region: Rock Stream · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
title: 2024 Apollo’s Praise Lahoma Vineyard Seneca Lake Scheurebe
about: Apollo’s Praise was founded in 2023 by the winemaking couple Kelby James Russell and Julia Rose Hoyle. Both started out in the tasting room at Fox Run on Seneca Lake before moving into production; Russell went on to be head winemaker at Red Newt Cellars, Hoyle at Hosmer. The name comes from “Glorious Apollo,” a song Russell sang with the Harvard Glee Club. In April 2023 the couple bought Lahoma Vineyard from the grower Ken Fulkerson: about 20 acres on the south-west side of Seneca Lake, near Rock Stream, whose Riesling Russell had made into celebrated single-vineyard wines at Red Newt.

Lahoma sits higher than most vinifera sites around the lake, at roughly 800–855 feet and above the shale that dominates its neighbours, on uncommon sandstone-derived Dunkirk and Odessa silt loams. It is also home to New York’s first planting of Scheurebe, a German variety, put in the ground in 2018. The 2024 grapes were picked by hand and fermented in neutral French barriques, rested on their lees for four months, then racked and finished for four more months in stainless steel. Only 122 cases were made.

The wine is dry, with just 2 g/L of residual sugar, and 12.5% alcohol. Scheurebe is prized for its perfume, and critics found the warm 2024 season made this vintage more aromatic than the last: James Suckling noted “off-the-scale” yellow grapefruit and a sea-salt character on a compact, medium-bodied palate, while Vinous described melon, peach, lychee, green tea and orange oil, tightening with air to a mineral finish. Our list notes mandarin, flint and bright lime.
